result.description:
Position: Telecommunications Technical Officer
Type: Full-time
Employer: Online Star PTY LTD
Location: Canberra ACT
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business
Online Star PTY LTD is a dynamic Canberra-based provider of telecommunications services and solutions, alongside IT services, dedicated to optimising business performance and unlocking new revenue streams in the rapidly evolving communications sector. With a team of highly experienced professionals, we partner with major telecom operators and vendors to deliver customised solutions that help clients enter new markets, defend existing ones, secure networks, improve quality, and deploy infrastructure efficiently. Our core values centre on innovation, operational excellence, cost-effectiveness, and high-quality service delivery, fostering a collaborative and supportive workplace culture where technical expertise drives tangible business outcomes and subscriber satisfaction.
About the Position
The Telecommunications Technical Officer plays a critical role at Online Star PTY LTD in supporting the delivery of NBN fibre and telecommunications network projects. This position involves field-based technical support, testing coordination, quality oversight and technical guidance across active project sites. The role sits between the Project Engineers and the field technicians and is essential to ensuring that network works are delivered to the required technical standards, that faults are diagnosed and rectified efficiently, and that completed works meet client acceptance requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Reviewing job packs, network plans, asset records and scopes of work before field work begins and confirming the design intent against site conditions.
Attending project sites to assess ground conditions, identify service and access risks, and confirm the scoped works can be built to the client design and NBN requirements.
Providing technical direction to field technicians during fibre hauling, splicing, pit and pipe works, exchange patching and BNTD installation.
Coordinating and verifying fibre testing using OTDR and optical power meters, and validating results against applicable NBN and client acceptance requirements before handover to the delivery partner.
Diagnosing fibre, duct, patching and connection faults on site, tracing the cause and setting out the rectification steps required to keep the job on schedule.
Checking completed works against the plans, job packs and NBN specifications, and confirming they are ready for submission to the project manager or delivery partner.
Preparing and updating as-built records, test results, site reports, defect notes and completion packs.
Coordinating with project engineers, supervisors, delivery partners, subcontractors and customers on site access, progress, technical issues and completion sign-off.
Monitoring crews on site to confirm they follow the approved work method, the SWMS and the relevant technical standards.
Escalating complex design, structural or safety matters to the Project Engineers or management where higher-level approval is required.
Reviewing rejected or non-compliant work, identifying why it failed, and instructing field crews on the correct method to bring it back to standard.
Keeping records of materials, equipment, test outcomes, network locations and work status to support project tracking and partner reporting.
Monitoring the performance of completed fibre network segments, interpreting transmission and optical test results, and identifying where network performance requires correction or improvement.
Configuring and integrating telecommunications network equipment, including BNTDs and related network access equipment, and verifying correct operation after installation.
Ensuring compliance with Work Health and Safety obligations on all project sites.
Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in a relevant field.
Minimum 1 year of relevant experience.
Strong technical skills in telecommunications network testing, fault diagnosis, equipment configuration and integration, including practical experience with OTDR and optical power meters.
Excellent problem-solving abilities, attention to detail, and the capacity to maintain accurate documentation and logs.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills for liaising with internal teams, delivery partners, vendors and clients.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with a focus on quality standards and operational efficiency.
How to Apply
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Job no: 944998

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Administration, Business and Management, Information-Communication Technology, Policy




 

Department for Health and Wellbeing - Commissioning and Performance - Activity Based Management and Funding

Salary: $116,089 to $125,490 - ASO7 - Full Time - Ongoing - Permanent

Overview:

The Revenue Policy Analyst is responsible for the development of revenue policy and strategy within the newly established Revenue Strategy Unit (RS). This is a great opportunity for team members currently working within Local Health Networks (LHNs) to contribute to system-wide policy development and gain experience within the Department. 

The unit supports and manages key policy initiatives designed to support the optimisation of revenue outcomes for public health services. The unit's purpose is to provide system leadership, though policy and guidance to revenue-based teams working across the Local Health Networks, who are responsible for optimising revenue outcomes and meeting revenue compliance requirements. It achieves this through:

The development and maintenance of policies and guidelines (policy and governance).

Strategy, education, and business reform across all patient revenue streams.

The provision of a level 2 helpdesk, supporting Local Health Networks to get policy and practice right every time.

Commonwealth department and jurisdictional consultation and engagement on system wide issues-matters.

Periodic and ad hoc Revenue Compliance reviews.

The Revenue Policy Analyst will be involved in funding matters and audits and the provision of expert policy related advice to Local Health Networks (LHNs) to ensure that SA Health policies are implemented and adhered to.

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

result.description:
Employer: Industrial Automation Group
Location: Joondalup, WA
Salary: $75,000 – $95,000 per annum plus superannuation
Employment Type: Full-Time

Industrial Automation Group is an innovative engineering and technology solutions provider specialising in automation, control systems, and Industrial IoT solutions. The company designs, develops, and delivers integrated engineering solutions to improve operational efficiency, asset performance, and system reliability across various industries.

With expertise in automation technologies, intelligent control systems, remote monitoring solutions, and engineering project delivery, IA Group provides customised solutions to meet complex operational requirements.

IA Group is seeking an experienced Automation and Control Engineer to join its engineering team on a full-time basis. The successful candidate will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and managing the design, implementation, modification, and ongoing performance of automation and control systems, equipment, and industrial plant solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Reviewing project requirements, functional specifications, operational processes, and technical information to determine system functions, engineering requirements, and improvement opportunities.
Analysing operational data, equipment performance, facility layouts, and production requirements to identify opportunities for improving system efficiency, reliability, and productivity.
Designing, developing, and implementing electrical, automation, and control systems for industrial automation projects, including configuring PLC, HMI, and SCADA systems to enable process monitoring, control, data acquisition, and reporting.
Developing and modifying PLC control programs using industry-standard programming methodologies, including function block diagrams, ladder logic, and IEC 61131-3 programming standards to optimise automated processes and equipment performance.
Preparing engineering specifications, technical documentation, system designs, and project reports, including determining suitable equipment, control components, system configurations, and installation requirements.
Performing system integration, testing, commissioning, and validation activities, including Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), to ensure automation systems meet design specifications and operational requirements.

Skills and Experience Required

To be successful in this role, you will have:

A Bachelor’s degree or higher qualification in Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Control Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related field.
Minimum of 2–3 years of demonstrated experience in industrial automation, control systems, and engineering project delivery.
Experience with PLC programming, HMI configuration, SCADA systems, and industrial control technologies.
Knowledge of automation system integration, commissioning, testing, and maintenance processes.
Ability to interpret engineering drawings, technical specifications, and system documentation.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify and resolve complex technical issues.

What We Offer
Full-time permanent employment opportunity.
Competitive salary package of $75,000 – $95,000 plus superannuation.
Opportunity to work on innovative industrial automation and engineering projects.
Supportive and professional engineering environment with opportunities for career development.

Apply Now:
If you are an experienced Automation and Control Engineer looking to contribute to innovative engineering solutions, please submit your application with your resume and relevant experience.
